reason: The signals identify the stem-cell subset's route toward muscle precursors, the starting point for making a muscle fibre.

reason: The fusion proteins match the membranes of adjacent myoblasts and should join them into a muscle fibre.

effect: The myoblasts fused and matured into fibres with actin–myosin units; their grip sites are still covered.

reason: The calcium pulse reaches the filaments and is the available signal for starting contraction.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites and the filaments slid; the fibre now needs calcium removed to become ready again.
reaction: The distinction between filament sliding and filament shortening is clear.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes should return calcium to storage and allow the fibre to relax.
expectation: ATP-powered pumps will remove calcium from around the filaments, allowing the grip sites to be covered again.

effect: Calcium pumping stopped pulling and completed the fibre goal; the next task is to assemble and attach both muscles.
reaction: It is useful to see that relaxation also requires ATP and an outside pull for lengthening.
reason: The empty biceps sheaths are designed to hold muscle fibres and connect them to tendons.
expectation: The fibres will fill the biceps sheaths to form a muscle with tendons.

reaction: The automatic correction clarified the missing assembly step.
reason: The fascicles can now fill the empty biceps sheaths and connect to their tendons.
expectation: The fascicles will form the biceps within its sheaths and tendons.

reaction: The force-path inset makes the tendon connection useful to follow.

reaction: The paired poses make the contrasting actions clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium-triggered contraction and reset were most worthwhile: the planned images distinguish sliding filaments from shortening filaments and show ATP's role in both release and calcium pumping.

leastWorthwhile.text: Assembling the second muscle was somewhat repetitive, though its three heads and different origins added anatomical detail.

surprise.text: The relaxed fibre lengthened under an outside pull, while ATP-powered calcium pumps stopped its pulling; relaxation was not simply the reverse of contraction.

arbitrary.text: I initially expected fibres to go directly into the biceps sheaths. The required extracellular-matrix step was not obvious beforehand, but the resulting connective layers gave it a clear purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the muscle-and-tendon force path connects to further body systems; the constructions gave useful structural explanations, though the assembly sequence could be predictable.
